observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

observation.setting: Outdoor stage with tatami mats at Heian Shrine in Kyoto, with traditional shrine architecture and spectators watching in the background
observation.dancers: Three women in the main performance group
observation.formation_and_space: In-line formation facing forward on a raised stage, holding stationary positions with minimal travel
observation.posture: Upright torso, upright posture with straight knees most of the time, lowering into a kneeling position near the end
observation.footwork: Cannot be seen under the long red skirts
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held out at various levels, holding ritual props including wooden fans and handheld branch-like items with long colorful ribbons dangling down
observation.hips_and_torso: Still torso with minimal movement except when bowing or kneeling
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Standing upright with graceful arm gestures, descending to kneel on the floor near the end
observation.costume_and_props: White over-garments (haori/kosode), bright red pleated skirts (hakama), gold ornate crowns, holding folding wooden fans and ritual staffs with ribbons
observation.cannot_infer: Footwork and lower body movements are entirely occluded by long traditional skirts.

signature_moments.what: Dancers slowly raise and lower arms, gently waving fan and ribbon props in coordination with flute and drum notes.
Dancers slowly lower themselves to kneel on the tatami mat while holding props upright.
